SubTopics: Recognize that energy is present when objects move; describe the effects of energy transfer from one object to another.
Content: A student investigated the energy transfer that happens when `text(two)` objects crash into each other during a collision. The student labeled `text(two)` identical balls as Ball `1` and Ball `2`. The student rolled Ball `1` toward Ball `2` on the floor. The figure shows the student's investigation.
problems/TN25G3S/media/1a.jpg
The student claims that Ball `1` transferred energy to Ball `2` because after the collision, Ball `2` began to move.
What additional evidence would `ultext(best)` support the student's claim?

A.Choice: The speed of Ball `1` increased after the collision.

B.Choice: The volume of Ball `1` increased after the collision.

C.Choice: The temperature of Ball `2` increased after the collision.

D.Choice: The mass of Ball `2` increased after the collision.

SubTopics: Explain the cause and effect relationship between a naturally changing environment and an organism's ability to survive.
Content: When Arctic sea ice melts in the `text(spring)`, nutrients enter the water. Tiny plantlike organisms use the nutrients to grow and reproduce. Animals called krill eat the plantlike organisms.
Scientists measure the amount of sea ice covering the Arctic sea `text(each September)`. The graph shows how the amount of Arctic sea ice has changed over time.
problems/TN25G3S/media/2a.jpg
What are `ultext(two)` ways in which the amount of nutrients, plantlike organisms, and krill will `ultext(most likely)` change in the `text(spring)` of `2030`?

A.Choice: Less nutrients will enter the water.

B.Choice: More nutrients will enter the water.

C.Choice: There will be fewer plantlike organisms and fewer krill.

D.Choice: There will be fewer plantlike organisms and more krill.

E.Choice: There will be more plantlike organisms and more krill.

SubTopics: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts electrical energy to another form of energy, using open or closed simple circuits.
Content: A student uses a battery to cause a light bulb to produce light. The light bulb produces a dim light. The figure shows the student's setup.
problems/TN25G3S/media/3a.jpg
Another student claims that adding a `text(second)` battery to the circuit would increase the brightness of the light bulb.
What reasoning `ultext(best)` supports the student's claim?

A.Choice: The circuit is currently open, and adding a `text(second)` battery would make it closed.

B.Choice: The circuit is currently closed, and adding a `text(second)` battery would make it open.

C.Choice: A `text(second)` battery would provide more energy that could be converted into light.

D.Choice: A `text(second)` battery would provide less energy that could be converted into light.

SubTopics: Analyze the internal and external structures that aquatic and land animals and plants have to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.
Content: The saguaro cactus lives in a very hot and dry desert environment. The figure shows a saguaro cactus.
problems/TN25G3S/media/5a.jpg
The table describes some saguaro cactus structures.
problems/TN25G3S/media/5b.jpg
Which `ultext(three)` structures `ultext(best)` help the saguaro cactus to survive in a very dry environment?

A.Choice: the roots, because they allow the cactus to collect water as soon as it rains

B.Choice: the stem, because it stores water for use during times when there is little rain

C.Choice: the spines, because they stop animals from eating the cactus

D.Choice: the skin, because it reduces the amount of water the cactus loses to the air

E.Choice: the flowers, because they attract animals that help spread the saguaro seeds across the desert

SubTopics: Explain the cause and effect relationship of magnets.
Content: A group of students designed an investigation to study magnetic forces. The students followed this procedure:

:ibox:• Use string to hang a bar magnet from a stand.

• Tie an iron paper clip to a `text(second)` string.

• Attach the `text(second)` string to a weight placed on the surface below the magnet.
The figure shows the students' investigation setup. The figure also shows the behavior of the paper clip.
problems/TN25G3S/media/8a.jpg
In which `ultext(two)` ways can the students change the investigation setup to increase the attraction between the magnet and the paper clip?

A.Choice: Increase the mass of the weight.

B.Choice: Replace the magnet with a stronger magnet.

C.Choice: Make the string attached to the paper clip longer.

D.Choice: Flip the magnet so the `text(south)` pole is facing the paper clip.

E.Choice: Replace the paper clip with a heavier paper clip.

SubTopics: Construct an argument to explain why some animals benefit from forming groups.
Content: Some species of fish swim in large groups called schools. Fish in schools move together and swim in different patterns or shapes. The figure shows a school of mackerel forming a sphere.
problems/TN25G3S/media/9a.jpg
Based on the figure, how does forming a sphere `ultext(most likely)` help a school of mackerel?

A.Choice: It helps all the fish swim faster.

B.Choice: It makes the water colder for the fish to survive.

C.Choice: It helps all the fish hunt for food.

D.Choice: It makes it harder for predators to capture the fish.

SubTopics: Use tables, graphs, and tools to describe precipitation, temperature, and wind (direction and speed) to determine local weather and climate.
Content: The table shows the usual temperature and precipitation for `text(four months)` in Nashville, Tennessee, from `1991` to `2020`. Temperature is measured in `text(degrees Fahrenheit)` (`°text(F)`).
problems/TN25G3S/media/10a.jpg
Based on the data in the table, which `ultext(two)` statements `ultext(most likely)` describe the temperature and precipitation in Nashville in `text(July 2018)`?

C.Choice: There was less than `3` `text(inches)` of precipitation.

E.Choice: There was more than `5` `text(inches)` of precipitation.

SubTopics: Infer that plant and animal adaptations help them survive in land and aquatic biomes.
Content: Honeybees are pollinators. Pollinators move pollen from `text(one)` flower to another. The model shows how a honeybee interacts with a plant.
problems/TN25G3S/media/11a.jpg
Honeybees live in groups called colonies. The table shows the number of honeybee colonies in the United States between `1970` and `2000`.
problems/TN25G3S/media/11b.jpg
Based on the information provided, how did the change in the honeybee population between `1970` and `2000` `ultext(most likely)` affect human resources?

A.Choice: An increase in the honeybee population probably caused an increase in the number of fruits produced for eating.

B.Choice: An increase in the honeybee population probably caused a decrease in the amount of pollen produced for growing new plants.

C.Choice: A decrease in the honeybee population probably caused a decrease in the number of fruits produced for eating.

D.Choice: A decrease in the honeybee population probably caused an increase in the amount of pollen produced for growing new plants.
